## The BB Gun Toddler & Parenting Agendas
A viral clip of a toddler wielding a BB gun has sparked a lively debate on Bluesky regarding child safety and modern parenting trends. Users are dissecting the footage to determine if the outburst was a result of environmental influence or active supervision strategies. While critics point to the sheer prevalence of toy guns in early childhood as evidence of shifting norms, others focus on the safety measures in place, such as the child wearing protective gear. The discussion ranges from humorous takes on the child’s aim to serious analysis of whether the environment fostered the behavior.

## YouTube’s A/B Testing Controversy
Bluesky users are rallying against YouTube’s new feature that allows creators to publish multiple video variations (A/B testing) under a single URL. The consensus is largely negative, with commenters calling it a "horrible idea" that artificially inflates view counts and ruins data transparency. Critics argue this enables deceptive practices, such as masquerading three separate videos as one to game algorithms. The discourse highlights concerns over unfairness for competitors and viewers alike, with some joking about a regression in platform integrity when YouTube will finally outlaw these manipulative thumbnail and title tests.

## Wild Hornets Fundraising Nears Goal
The "Wild Hornets" campaign to support Ukraine’s 12th Special Operations Center is making significant progress. The initiative has raised $8,280 toward its $17,600 goal, aiming to purchase three Hornet Vision CTRL stations. These stations will allow remote operation of STING interceptors to shoot down Russian Shahed drones over Kharkiv. To boost donations, organizers have introduced a raffle structure: $10 entry fees or merchandise purchases grant tickets. A $500 tier offers a guaranteed strike video and the chance to name a specific STING interceptor. Participants are sending screenshots of donations to designated accounts like @wendehopes or @koadre to receive tickets.

## Games & Vintage Days 2026 Schedule
Jakub 'borg' Rzepecki announced the full schedule for Games & Vintage Days 2026, taking place October 10-11 in Wrocław. The event features three stages with keynotes from *Deluxe Ski Jump* creator Jussi Koskela and Polish journalist Waldemar “Pegaz Ass” Nowak. Highlights include GOG.com’s Piotr Gnyp discussing digital heritage preservation and live-coding challenges, such as rewriting *River Raid* in 45 minutes. The agenda also covers Polish retro-computing culture, market failures like the Philips CD-i, and the legal aspects of fan adaptations.

## Photography Community Insights
On 4chan’s /p/ board, photographers are debating techniques for bird photography, recommending custom ISO limits and single-point autofocus for better control. Meanwhile, discussions on upcoming gear focus on Nikon’s rumored Z5IIC, a compact full-frame camera designed to compete with Sony’s a7c series. While the lack of an electronic viewfinder has some calling it "worthless" for bright conditions, others are excited for a non-Sony option. Elsewhere, a photographer seeks advice on disassembling a Sigma 15mm f/2.8 lens to fix noisy autofocus issues following a remote service repair.

## Gaming & Retro Tech
A *Star Ocean Second Story R* player shares their experience as an JRPG newbie with ADHD, praising the game’s improved guidance. They seek clarification on battle mechanics for the character Rena and look for recommendations similar to *Final Fantasy 16* or *Nier: Automata*. In the retro space, a video by La Synthèse Humaine explores Roland Kayn’s cybernetic music experiments at Utrecht’s Instituut voor Sonologie, specifically his use of Léo Küpper’s home-built GAME synthesizer for the piece *Simultan*.

## Quick Hits

*   **Japan’s Tourist Shift:** On /trv/, users argue Japan is "healing" from overtourism as Chinese visitors drop more sharply than Americans. One French poster notes that current Chinese tourists are quieter and less obtrusive than UK "britbongs" or Australian backpackers.
*   **Moon Photography Artifacts:** /p/ users analyze stacked lunar images, noting that while software processing improves sharpness, it introduces a noticeable mosaic pattern.
*   **Digital Exhaustion:** A lone post from @Demigirlboss captures a moment of definitive fatigue with the simple declaration, "I'm not fucking doing this."
*   **Switch 2 Hesitation:** The JRPG player notes they are undecided on the Switch 2, balancing the desire for accessible combat against the price differences between Switch and PS4/5 games.

representative_texts: @Humble_Tonight_1675 - Photography community ready to help. — Problema AF de Sigma 15mm F2.8, alguém pode ajudar a abri-la? — Fala, pessoal! Beleza?   Tinha uma Sigma 15mm f/2.8 usada que estava com o diafragma travado, mas o AF era perfeito   Mandei para um técnico, o diafragma voltou a funcionar, mas o autofoco parou totalmente. Levei de volta para ele corrigir o AF e recebi a lente com o AF funcionando, mas com o seguinte B.O   No Autofoco (AF): O motor está fazendo um barulho bem mais alto que o normal, a lente vibra mais que o normal (como se estivesse fazendo força excessiva) e a busca de foco está ligeiramente mais lenta.   O foco em si funciona perfeitamente, parece só uma questão de engrenagens ou algo relacionado (da minha visão de super leigo). Enfim, o problema é o barulho e apesar da ligeira lentidão que não existia. O foco é perfeito   No Foco Manual (MF): O anel de foco gira perfeitamente liso, sem travamentos ou resistência.   Isso me faz pensar que talvez seja algo mais superficial, não achei nenhum guia na internet ensinando a abri-la. Então a ideia do posto é saber se vocês conseguem me ajudar com isso? Quero ver se talvez eu não de sorte de ser só um reparo simples que eu possa fazer em casa. E aí de repente com algumas dicas de vocês eu mesmo de uma olhadinha e veja uma coisa ou outra.   Obs: eu não posso levar de volta ao técnico porque ele é de outra cidade e toda vez que volto nele tenho que arcar com gastos rodoviários   Posted by u/Humble_Tonight_1675 · [comments]
clusters.summary: A user named @Humble_Tonight_1675 is seeking advice from the photography community on how to disassemble a used Sigma 15mm f/2.8 lens to perform a home repair. The lens was recently serviced by a technician in another city to fix a stuck aperture, but after the return, the autofocus (AF) began making excessive noise, vibrating heavily, and operating slower than before, despite focusing correctly. While manual focus (MF) works perfectly smooth, the user suspects an internal gear issue might be resolved with a simple fix, noting they cannot return the lens due to travel costs. The post highlights the frustration of remote service complications and invites fellow photographers to provide disassembly guides or troubleshooting tips for this specific model.

representative_texts: @matrix (noreply@blogger.com) - MATRIXSYNTH — Simultan, Léo Küpper, and Cybernetic Expansion — video upload by La Synthèse Humaine "In 1970 Roland Kayn moved to the Netherlands and began working at the Instituut voor Sonologie in Utrecht with two very important people - Jaap Vink and Léo Küpper. There he began to refine and expand his ideas of cybernetic music and his first large scale piece was Simultan - realized primarily in Bruxelles using Léo Küpper's home built GAME (Générateur
clusters.summary: A recent video upload by La Synthèse Humaine explores the collaborative work of Roland Kayn, Léo Küpper, and the concept of Cybernetic Expansion. The content highlights Kayn’s move to the Netherlands in 1970 to work at the Instituut voor Sonologie in Utrecht alongside Jaap Vink and Léo Küpper. During this period, Kayn refined his cybernetic music ideas, resulting in his first large-scale piece, *Simultan*. Notably, *Simultan* was primarily realized in Brussels using Léo Küpper’s home-built GAME (Générateur d'Automa te Musical Électronique), marking a significant technological milestone in the project's execution.

representative_texts: @Jakub 'borg' Rzepecki (borg@wspanialy.eu) — Dopięliśmy wszystko na ostatni guzik i z dumą oddajemy w Wasze ręce tegoroczny harmonogram prelekcji, dyskusji i spotkań Games & Vintage Days 2026! Podzieliliśmy nasz program na scenę główną oraz dwie prelekcyjne, dbając o to, by każdy pasjonat dawnej szkoły gamingu znalazł coś dla siebie. Prawdziwym świętem będą dla nas spotkania z legendami - na naszej scenie pojawi się m.in. sam Jussi Koskela, twórca kultowego Deluxe Ski Jump, który ukształtował dzieciństwo całego pokolenia, a także ikona polskiego dziennikarstwa growego, Waldemar „Pegaz Ass” Nowak. Nie zabraknie też ważnych dyskusji branżowych: razem z przedstawicielem GOG.com Piotrem Gnypem przyjrzymy się ratowaniu cyfrowego dziedzictwa w ramach „Cyfrowej Arki Noego”, a twórcy z RetroGralni (borg i mfx) opowiedzą o kulisach powstawania formatu „Weź Przewiń”. Będzie także okazja, by posłuchać prelekcji Krzysztofa „NRGeeka” Micielskiego oraz Łukasza „Zmasło” Zmysła i Marcela „WPM” Halczyńskiego. Przygotowaliśmy również mocny blok techniczny i scenowy, w którym nostalgia zderzy się z żywym kodem. Odwiedzający zobaczą m.in. karkołomną próbę przepisania River Raid w zaledwie 45 minut w formule live-codingu, zagłębią się w fascynujący i tajemniczy świat systemu TempleOS, a także przyjrzą się demoscenie oraz pojedynkowi nowoczesnych wcieleń Amigi. Obok czystej inżynierii sporo miejsca poświęcimy specyfice polskich realiów z minionych dekad. Wspólnie wrócimy do klimatu giełd komputerowych i ery kasetowego piractwa, odwiedzimy duszne salony gier zręcznościowych z lat 70., 80. i 90., a także porozmawiamy o psychologii stojącej za kupowaniem „dzieciństwa, którego nie mieliśmy”. Nie uciekamy też od tematów niszowych, kuriozalnych czy wręcz przeznaczonych wyłącznie dla dorosłych. W planie znalazły się rozliczenia z rynkowymi porażkami pokroju konsoli Philips CD-i, analiza wielkiego krachu branży z 1983 roku, a także wieczorny panel o raczkującej erotyce w grach lat 70. i 80. Całość dopełnią analizy prawne dotyczące fanowskich adaptacji retro oraz przegląd nowych, fizycznych wydań na Atari czy Commodore 64. Mamy nadzieję, że nasza siatka programowa dostarczy Wam tylu emocji podczas słuchania, ile nam dało jej układanie – pełny harmonogram godzinowy czeka już na Was na naszej stronie! Tabela z programem: https:// gamesvintagedays.pl/edycja-202 6/program/ 🕹️ Zapraszamy na: Games & Vintage Days 2026 🕹️ 💾 Termin: 10-11 października 2026 💾 🧙‍♀️ Miejsce: Czasoprzestrzeń, Wrocław 🧙‍♀️ ❤️ Strona: https://www. gamesvintagedays.pl # retrogaming  # giereczkowo  # retrocomputing
clusters.summary: Jakub 'borg' Rzepecki announced the full schedule for Games & Vintage Days 2026, taking place on October 10-11, 2026, at Czasoprzestrzeń in Wrocław. The event features a diverse program split across three stages, headlined by keynote speakers such as Jussi Koskela, creator of *Deluxe Ski Jump*, and Polish gaming journalist Waldemar “Pegaz Ass” Nowak. Key discussions include GOG.com’s Piotr Gnyp on preserving digital heritage in “Cypher Ark of Noah” and RetroGralni creators detailing the *Weź Przewiń* format. Attendees will witness live-coding challenges, including rewriting *River Raid* in 45 minutes, alongside explorations of TempleOS and Amiga demos. The agenda also covers Polish retro-computing culture, market failures like the Philips CD-i, the 1983 crash, and legal aspects of fan adaptations.

clusters.summary: User @Velokieken shares their experience with *Star Ocean Second Story R*, noting they are a JRPG newbie who struggles with complex systems due to ADHD but appreciates the game's improved guidance and manual-like features. The player has recruited several characters, including Opera and Rena, and seeks clarification on battle mechanics, specifically whether calling a benched Rena will heal or attack based on her settings. They also inquire about upgrading Rena’s familiar level to four and improving gear crafting, while mentioning missed content like private interactions with Ashton. In search of similar recommendations, the user prefers grindable, non-open-world titles like *Final Fantasy 16*, *Persona 5 Strikers*, and *Nier: Automata*, favoring the Nintendo Switch for its pause functionality despite higher prices. They remain undecided on the Switch 2, balancing a desire for accessible combat against the cost differences between Switch and PS4/5 games.
